Script:


Witness to power Final Script for TX Sunday 10th November 2024

Voice over 1
He is a published author of Afrikaans poetry. He is also a former MK soldier trained in East Germany.

Govan
It’s weird, an Umkhonto Wesizwe soldier becoming an Afrikaans author?
Mathews
I was that before I was MK. I published poems in Afrikaans when I was sixteen.

Voice over 2
Now, this former ANC treasurer General who raised well over R250 million for the ANC under Jacob Zuma, has written his political memoir.

Link
Mathews Phosa calls his book Witness to power but he was much more than that - since 1994 he was influencing South Africa’s defining political moments

Govan
Why didn’t you go into your running the ANC a bit more in the book?
Matthews
Because there will be a place for that …I have my agenda and you will be there
Govan
What is your agenda Mr Phosa?
Mathews
My agenda is to tell the truth.
Govan
In incremental bits?
Mathews
No, the way I want to.
Govan
Well I think you are still very close to people who wield power?
Mathews
Who me?
Yes
Matthews
Extremely close. Extremely close

FADE TO BLACK

Voice over 3
He has had a close relationship with every president since 1994.


But in 2001, Phosa became one of three ANC veterans accused by then president, Thabo Mbeki of a plot to topple him.


Six years later Phosa tabled a motion to remove Mbeki at Polokwane

Govan
What did you think of the government he built after the Mandela presidency?
Mathews
Mbeki?
Yes.
He did very well, the economy grew that time, when he was president, there was confidence
Govan
And yet you were instrumental in removing him from government?
Matthews
Well politics moves like a river, the water flows. Remember him and Steve Tshwete accused me, Tokyo Sexwale and Cyril Ramaphosa of plotting not only to overthrow him but kill him! A thing unimaginable!
He made one mistake Mbeki with all the good things he did.
Govan
He took you on? [laughs]
Phosa
No no, not only me. He took everyone on. He started to do what Machiavelli calls lopping off the top. He saw enemies where there were no enemies

Voice over 4
Phosa writes: “There was no winner at Polokwane. The ANC was the biggest loser. It lost its unity, cohesion and moral high ground and the deep wounds opened at that conference are still haemorrhaging.”

Up sound ZUMA

Voice over 5
In 2009 Jacob Zuma was inaugurated as President of the country.
In this interview from the Carte Blanche archive, Phosa’s support was unequivocal

Up sound Matthews Carte Blanche archive
Jacob Zuma is a very nice uncle, a very simple man, who appeals to us because of the accessibility, and he doesn't pretend to be what he is not

Govan
What did you anticipate from the Zuma government?
Mathews Phosa
Well you know we thought Zuma would run the country in terms of the constitution and follow the rule of law. We thought so.

Up sound So help me God

LINK
When it comes to Zuma, Phosa feels a mix of regret and betrayal. Regret because he didn't spot Zuma’s ways earlier and betrayal because the man that recruited him into the ANC ended up breaking away from the party and starting uMkhonto weSizwe and decimating ANC support…

Govan
You trained in East Germany?
Yes.
Govan
I ask that, to ask your opinion of the formation of the MK party then, since you are yourself a real MK soldier?
Mathews
Well the person who launched the party was a former president of the ANC and of SA. He condemned anyone who betrayed the ANC. He has come to walk on his own words. So he broke his own oath in the ANC

Voice over 6
As ANC treasurer, raising funds was Phosa’s job, it wasn't long, he writes before Jacob Zuma took him to meet his friends, and the family allegedly at the centre of state capture, the Gupta’s.

Matthews
He introduced me to them. I didn’t know who they were. I had never heard of them and I drove behind him until we reached these big gates there. So we discussed money in that house, I said guys my job is to raise funds for the ANC. No other job except that one.
Govan
And they gave you money? The ANC?
Mathews
No! No! They never gave me a cent.
Govan
They gave the ANC money?
I don’t know! They say so!
Govan
But you were the treasurer?
Matthews
But they didn’t give it to me! I didn’t receive one cent from the Gupta’s for the ANC. Never!

Voice over 7
But he does recount bumping into one of the Gupta brothers, Tony at a Durban hotel where he asked when he could expect their contribution. Gupta said they gave Baba R20 million.


Govan
Why didn’t you raise your hand against the Guptas in the ANC meetings early on.
Mathews
I did. And they hated me. I was an enemy to them at that time, because I was not doing their biddings.

Voice over 8
As a post revolutionary party, the ANC had friendships with countries that were often considered disreputable by the west. Libyan autocrat Muamar Gaddafi was one such character

Link
For years the ANC denied they had received money from Muamar Gaddafi but now Phosa says he opened channels for funding for the ANC throughout the middle east

Phosa
The whole Middle East gave me money. I opened a chapter with the arab world that did not exist in funding the ANC.
Govan
You opened that chapter?
Mathews
Yes I did! I am much more deeper than you can imagine! And they supported me. I got support from the UAE, I mean all over, all over.

Voice over 9
Phosa shied away from naming which middle eastern countries continue to fund the ANC

Mathews
I am not going to disclose them because they are still helping us, some of them
Govan
Are they still helping you, because I am trying to recall whether I have seen any disclosure of political party funding from Middle Eastern countries?
Phosa
I can tell you, that bill was started by me as treasurer/ about the need /to say what we are getting from who. I originated that law
Govan
It's such an important piece of legislation, one of the most progressive in recent times
Phosa
Thank you very much!
Govan
And yet it perplexes me as to why you wouldn't want to say now then?
Matthews
No no I talk about the law as it was …Let's be fair to me.

Voice over 10
Just two years before his assassination, Gaddafi made a substantial contribution to the ANC’s 2009 election campaign.

Govan
How much did you get from Gaddafi?
Matthews
I am not going to disclose that
Govan
You can estimate Mr Phosa
Matthews
No I will die with that secret in my coffin

Voice over 11
Another unsolved mystery is that of the mysterious Libyan billions: a plane full of money and gold rumoured to have been sent to South Africa shortly after Gaddafi’s death.

Phosa
I heard the story it's like King Solomon' s mines

Voice over 12
Phosa recalls how both the Libyans, and the CIA visited the ANC, looking for the loot

Govan
It's much more than a story Mr Phosa? Did you meet with the CIA over it?
Phosa
Me being the treasurer they came to ask me. I said I don't know anything
Govan
Did you track the money?
Phosa
What I did, I will tell you. There was an allegation the money was in a Swazi bank. I knew the governor of the reserve bank of Swaziland. I phoned him. He said we don’t know anything about Gaddafi money we know nothing, so what do I do when a governor says he knows nothing?

Voice over 13
By 2016 the press was filled with allegations of corruption and state capture that implicated the President. Phosa could no longer ignore them

Govan
When did your opinion of Jacob Zuma as the head of state change?
Mathews Phosa
Nkandla broke the camel’s neck for me. I couldn’t take it. State money was used to build it, and it was wrong because he had a state house.



Voice over 14
The Constitutional Court found Zuma had failed to defend, uphold, and respect the Constitution when using state funds on his sprawling Nkandla homestead.

Govan
At that point you would have with hindsight looked at how you would have been close to him over years and supported him. Do you regret that?
Mathews
I do. I do. What do you do when people show you their true colours? I went, why did I support this guy?

Voice over 15
Phosa called for Zuma to step down. Zuma iced him out.

Govan
You said you didn’t speak to the former president for five years?
Mathews
Maybe more.

Voice over 16
But unexpectedly the night before the ANC was going to remove President Zuma from office Phosa received a call

It was one of the President's body guards.

Phosa
I was in my pyjamas, the call came through that I must go to Mahlamba Ndlopfu. I must drive there at night…. I thought Matthew you are a soldier

Voice over 17
Phosa is a lawyer, and the president broke the years of silence to ask him for legal advice.

Matthews
I said Mr. president …….I love you, but I think you must step down

Voice over 18
In Feb 2018 Cyril Ramaphosa was first inaugurated as President.
In 2024 Zuma exacted his revenge.

Phosa writes that the formation of the MK party was a deliberate, calculated move by Zuma to get back at the man who succeeded him.

Matthews
MK was a big bomb on us!
Govan
What do you think MK will do to the ANC?
Mathews
I think MK will haemorrhage the ANC. Zuma is good at playing the victim. He is a master and now he has gone beyond that. He has become the Ayatollah of MK if I may use the word. But the reality is that MK is going to irritate all the political parties, especially the ANC.


Voice over 19
The MK party captured a chunk of the ANC’s support forcing Ramaphosa into a government of National Unity.

Govan
What do you think of his political leadership
Matthews
He is having challenges he can’t overcome easily
Govan
Do you think he is a good ANC president?
Matthews
I think he is too indecisive.

Voice over 20
Phosa rejects the idea that he is trying to whitewash his legacy and says he has written this memoir to fill in the spaces of history.

Govan
It seems like you are shifting power or influencing it behind the scenes?
Mathews
He smiles. I am not immobile in politics but I don’t intervene where I don’t have to intervene
Govan
Will you go back?
Matthews
I don't know, time will tell.

Voice over 21
As Phosa likes to say, politics is the art of the possible.

THE END


PROMO ONE

Mathews Phosa has just written his political memoir

Govan
Why didn’t you go into your running the ANC a bit more in the book?
Matthews
Because there will be a place for that …I have my agenda and you will be there
Govan
What is your agenda Mr Phosa?
Mathews
My agenda is to tell the truth.

PROMO TWO

Voice over
We sit down with former ANC politician Matthews Phosa to discuss his new political memoir.
Govan
How much did you get from Gaddafi?
Matthews
I am not going to disclose that
Govan
You can estimate Mr Phosa
Matthews
No I will die with that secret in my coffin
Why?
Because I am a disciplined member of my organisation


PROMO THREE
Mathews Phosa was recruited into the ANC by Jacob Zuma and was loyal to the former president, until he could no longer ignore his betrayal

Govan
Do you regret that?
Mathews
I do. I do. What do you do when people show you their true colours? I sad but why did I support this guy?

















































































































































































Shorter
